item.title: Interviewing for Oral History
item.description: Interview a former textile mill worker for a fictional oral history project. Help her tell the story in her own words, keep track of what was recorded, and agree on who may hear it.

children.definition: A short remark or cue that helps someone begin or continue speaking.
children.example: When Rosa struggled to get started, I offered a simple prompt: “Think about your first morning at the mill.”
children.translation_ru: вопрос или реплика, помогающие начать или продолжить рассказ
children.translation_uz: gapni boshlashga yoki davom ettirishga yordam beradigan savol yoki qisqa gap

children.definition: A memory of something that happened in the past.
children.example: Rosa’s clearest recollection of her first day was the noise of the looms.

children.definition: A document on which someone formally agrees to take part in an activity or allow their contribution to be used.
children.example: The consent form let Rosa agree to be recorded while deciding separately whether the project could publish her words.

children.definition: With the understanding that what someone says will be kept private and left out of anything published.
children.example: When Rosa asked to speak off the record about a former supervisor, I stopped the recording before she continued.

children.definition: A short period of silence before someone starts speaking again.
children.example: There was a long pause before Rosa described her last visit to the mill.

children.definition: A rule that limits who can see or hear material or when they may do so.
children.example: Rosa chose an access restriction that let project staff hear the recording but kept it from the public for five years.

children.definition: To contact someone again after a conversation to ask for more information or deal with an unfinished matter.
children.example: I said I would follow up with Rosa the next day to confirm which passage she wanted us to leave out.
children.translation_ru: снова связаться, чтобы уточнить детали или решить оставшийся вопрос
children.translation_uz: tafsilotlarga aniqlik kiritish yoki ochiq qolgan masalani hal qilish uchun yana bogʻlanmoq

children.definition: The person who tells the story of their own life or past events in an oral history project.
children.example: Rosa was the first narrator in the mill project to describe what night work was like.

children.definition: A written set of subjects to cover in a planned conversation.
children.example: My topic list included Rosa’s training, night work, and the day the mill shut down.
collocations: add something to the topic list

children.definition: Sound that has been captured and saved so it can be played back.
children.example: In the recording, you can hear Rosa laugh as she describes learning to use her first loom.

children.definition: To cancel the approval you previously gave for someone to do or use something.
children.example: Under our agreement, Rosa could withdraw permission to publish her story at any point before it went live.
collocations: withdraw permission to use a quotation

children.definition: A short part taken from a longer text, speech, or piece of audio.
children.example: Rosa approved a short excerpt about her first week at the mill for the exhibition.

children.definition: A name someone uses in public in place of their real name.
children.example: At the narrator's request, we used a pseudonym in the published transcript.

children.definition: To make the meaning of something easier to understand by explaining it more precisely.
children.example: Before moving on, I asked Rosa to clarify what she meant by “the old mill,” since two mills had operated in the town.
